- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often underestimates upside; add 3–5% to forecast for momentum continuation.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above recent high for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in correction; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 2–3 days.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% from forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >10% above model, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–10 days unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is high and price is flat or slightly declining, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
